transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Time: 3:00 PM PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Cruz (CTO, Oceanic Medical), Marcus Lee (Head of Ops), Sofia Ramos (Security Engineer)

Summary (auto): Quick security posture discovery to validate hosted vs dedicated vs private options, discuss SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention and next steps for pilot.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Ravi, our solutions engineer. Um we'll run about 30-45 minutes, want to hear your current stack and security reqs and then go through how Redwood handles things. 
[00:12] Dr. Elena Cruz: Thanks, Maya. I'm Elena, CTO at Oceanic. We're evaluating options for inference for some patient-facing summarization workflows. Primary concerns are PHI handling, so data residency, KMS, and audit logs.
[00:25] Marcus Lee: Hi, Marcus here. We're the ops lead, mainly interested in latency and cost tradeoffs. Also need to know how we'd integrate with Okta for SSO.
[00:32] Ravi Patel: Great, quick high level: Redwood has Hosted (our public API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra), and Private (VPC/air-gapped on-prem options). For PHI you typically look at Dedicated or Private depending on compliance and networking needs. Hosted can work with contractual safeguards but we understand many healthcare folks prefer private networks.
[00:52] Sofia Ramos: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs? We need Type II SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts for our vendor review.
[01:00] Maya Chen: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. I'll share the reports and a redacted summary after the call. We can also provide an info sec package with pen test results and our responsible disclosure policy.
[01:10] Dr. Elena Cruz: Great. On encryption: do you support BYOK or bring-your-own-key with HSM, and can we control key rotation?
[01:18] Ravi Patel: For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and a Redwood-managed KMS by default; we also support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers for Dedicated and Private—so you can bring keys in and we support HSM-backed keys in the private deployment. Key rotation can be managed per your policy, and we can document the rotation steps.
[01:35] Marcus Lee: If we use Dedicated, is network traffic e2e encrypted and can we restrict egress? We need to prevent any token or data leakage to public endpoints.
[01:45] Ravi Patel: Yes, TLS everywhere. With Dedicated you get isolated GPU pools and you can enforce network policies; with Private (VPC) you can peer directly to your VPC and lock down egress. We also have options for denying outbound requests by default and controlled endpoints for telemetry.
[02:02] Dr. Elena Cruz: Audit logs—what's your retention and granularity? We need per-request audit trails including user identity, request metadata, model/version used, and token counts for billing and compliance.
[02:13] Maya Chen: We capture per-request logs with timestamps, model ID, route, token usage, and request IDs. Default retention is 90 days in Hosted, but we can extend retention as an add-on for Dedicated/Private customers; for Private you control retention fully. We can also push logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[02:30] Sofia Ramos: For SSO we use Okta with SCIM provisioning and SAML. How's RBAC modeled? Do you have least-privilege roles and audit of admin actions?
[02:40] Ravi Patel: Yes, we support SAML SSO plus SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC has built-in roles (admin, developer, billing, auditor) and you can create custom roles with fine-grained permissions on routes, models, and environments. All admin actions are logged, and we provide an audit trail for changes to policies and rollouts.
[02:55] Dr. Elena Cruz: Is there MFA enforced for all console access?
[02:58] Maya Chen: We recommend MFA; for Hosted/Console we enforce MFA for all Redwood employees via SSO and we can require SSO-enforced MFA for your org. For Private deployments, you control your IdP policies.
[03:08] Marcus Lee: About data in transit vs rest—are embeddings/token caches persisted, and do you store any customer prompts in plaintext?
[03:16] Ravi Patel: Default behavior is ephemeral KV cache for inference to speed up subsequent requests; for Hosted we don't persist prompts to long-term storage for model input unless you enable logging for debugging/quality. When logging is enabled, data is encrypted at rest and in transit. For Dedicated/Private you have more control; we can disable logging entirely or forward logs to your systems.
[03:36] Dr. Elena Cruz: If we need to prove separation for auditors, can you provide architecture diagrams and SOC 2 scope details showing isolation between tenants?
[03:44] Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll include architecture diagrams and the portion of our SOC 2 report that explains multi-tenancy and segmentation. For Dedicated we can show the isolation at pool level and network controls.
[03:56] Sofia Ramos: Any known gaps re: HIPAA specifically? Do you have a BAA?
[03:59] Maya Chen: We do offer a BAA for healthcare customers; our legal team can execute it as part of contract discussions. There are operational controls we document in the BAAs—I'll flag legal follow-up.
[04:12] Marcus Lee: Performance question — if we run a pilot on Dedicated, can we run a short benchmark to validate P95 latency at our target sequence lengths? Also, how do quantization/FP16 affect accuracy for our clinical models?
[04:23] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can run a one-hour benchmark on a Dedicated pool with representative prompts. We'll provide profiling (latency distributions, token throughput). On quantization: we recommend model-specific testing; for many encoder-decoder and causal models, int8 or int4 profiles are supported, but there may be small quality delta. We'll include recommended quantization profiles and guidance for your eval set.
[04:45] Dr. Elena Cruz: About model governance — can we pin model versions and prevent automatic rollouts? We need deterministic behavior during validation.
[04:53] Ravi Patel: Yes, you can pin model versions and use rollout policies — canary, A/B, or manual promotion. Automatic rollouts are opt-in.
[04:59] (crosstalk)
[05:02] Marcus Lee: On incident response — do you share postmortems and notifications to customers? How quickly?
[05:08] Maya Chen: We have an incident response process with customer notifications for Sev2/Sev1 events within our SLA windows; we share postmortems and remediation steps, and for Dedicated/Private customers we offer a higher notification cadence based on contract.
[05:20] Sofia Ramos: Are there any limitations on data residency—like regions you don't support? We are required to keep prod data in us-east-1 or our on-prem.
[05:28] Ravi Patel: We have deployments in major cloud regions; for Hosted we have region options and for Dedicated you can choose region placement. For strict residency you can opt for Private on-prem or VPC in your chosen region.
[05:40] Dr. Elena Cruz: One more: do you support deletion APIs for data covered by requests (right to be forgotten)?
[05:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we provide deletion APIs and can coordinate purges of logs or telemetry per contract. For Hosted we have documented processes; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and deletions.
[05:55] Marcus Lee: Cost-policy question: if we enable longer audit logs retention or BYOK, does that add to monthly costs?
[06:00] Maya Chen: Yes, extended log retention and add-on security features are billed separately; we'll include a pricing appendix. Dedicated has capacity commit pricing which makes unit costs predictable.
[06:10] Dr. Elena Cruz: Timeline—what's realistic if we wanted a pilot with Dedicated and SOC review? We're aiming to start pilot by mid-March.
[06:16] Ravi Patel: We can provision a Dedicated pool in 2-3 weeks post agreement, so a mid-March pilot is realistic if legal and procurement move quickly. We'll coordinate security docs and a one-hour benchmark as part of the pilot.
[06:30] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and security pack, Ravi will share VPC/private deployment diagram and pilot plan, and we'll propose slots for the benchmark next week of March 2. Any final Qs?
[06:44] Dr. Elena Cruz: No, thanks that's good. We'll review and Sofia will send follow-up questions.
[06:50] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with docs and calendar invites.
